items.q: A cake is cut into 4 equal parts. You take 3 of the parts. What fraction of the cake did you take?
misconceptions: flipped the fraction: the cutting number goes on the bottom
counted only one part instead of the three taken
correct
named the count of parts with no whole behind it

items.q: A number line runs from 0 to 1 and is cut into 4 equal parts. Where does 3/4 sit?
misconceptions: counted the end of the line as a part: the fourth mark is the whole
placed it by feel: halfway is 2/4, not 3/4
read the top number as bigger than the whole
correct

items.q: In the fraction 5/8, what does the 8 tell you?
choices: The whole was cut into 8 equal parts
Each part is 8 times the whole
misconceptions: swapped the jobs: the top number counts what you take
turned the cutting number into a count of wholes
correct
grew the part bigger than the whole it came from

items.q: Which fraction is the same as 1/2?
misconceptions: kept the top number and changed the share
that is a whole one, not a half
correct
changed both numbers without re-slicing evenly
picked the bigger digits: 3 and 8 look bigger than 1 and 2
stopped at the counts without checking piece sizes
gave up before using the halfway benchmark
correct

items.q: Two cakes are the same size. Which serving is more: 2/3 of a cake or 2/4 of a cake?
misconceptions: picked the bigger bottom number: fourths are smaller pieces than thirds
matched the top numbers and stopped: same count, different piece sizes
correct
let the cutting order decide instead of the piece sizes
added the bottoms too: piece sizes do not add
dropped the piece size and kept only the count
added the top number twice instead of the two shares
correct
the Jumble answer: added the tops and the bottoms
added the tops but never re-sliced the half
correct
shrunk both shares to the smaller piece count

items.q: Sam ate 1/3 of a pizza. Jo ate 1/6 of the same pizza. How much pizza did they eat in all?
misconceptions: added the tops and the bottoms: the Jumble move
added the tops and kept one bottom: no re-slicing happened
multiplied the bottoms and guessed the top
correct
